topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students and outlines the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of the inflammatory response.

topics.label: Pathogen-associated and damage-associated molecular patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the foundational concepts of microbial and cellular damage detection through molecular patterns and how the immune system distinguishes self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptors and signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genetics, cellular localization, receptor families, and intracellular activation cascades, including the inflammasome, used to sense danger signals.

topics.label: Cellular recruitment, trafficking, and systemic inflammatory effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells, endothelial interactions, leukocyte extravasation, lymphatic drainage, and systemic mediator release coordinate the inflammatory reaction.

topics.label: Inflammation resolution, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the inflammatory response is terminated, how damaged tissue is healed, and how chronic states or granulomas arise when resolution is incomplete.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and announces the subject of the upcoming lecture.
